title: Day 601 — First Formal U.S.–Mexico USMCA Bilateral Review Round Opens in Mexico City
detail: On May 25, 2026 (Day 601), the first official bilateral U.S.–Mexico USMCA Review negotiating round opened in Mexico City, as agreed by USTR Ambassador Jamieson Greer and Mexican Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard in their joint statement (April 2026). This opens the substantive phase of USMCA renegotiation — the July 1, 2026 decision deadline under the treaty's six-year review clause approaches. KEY ISSUES: (1) RULES OF ORIGIN: The U.S. seeks stricter automotive content requirements to ensure vehicles meet North American origin thresholds and are not assembled from Chinese-origin parts through Mexican supply chains. (2) CHINESE NEARSHORING: USTR Greer has declared that preventing Chinese companies from exploiting Mexico as a tariff-free backdoor to the U.S. market is a 'non-negotiable' U.S. demand, requiring enhanced monitoring of foreign investment in Mexican manufacturing. (3) STEEL AND ALUMINUM TARIFFS: Mexico seeks termination of Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs on Mexican exports, which it views as inconsistent with USMCA's spirit. The U.S. confirmed these tariffs remain in place during talks. (4) ENERGY ACCESS: The U.S. is pushing for expanded access to Mexico's electricity and oil sectors, which Sheinbaum has defended as sovereign state prerogatives under the constitutional energy reform. (5) LABOR STANDARDS: Enforcement of the 2019 labor reform (rapid response mechanism) and new collective bargaining requirements continue to be evaluated. CANADA EXCLUDED: The current bilateral round is a Mexico-U.S.-only discussion; Canada is expected to join the full trilateral USMCA Joint Review scheduled for July 1, 2026. Greer also met with Mexico's Business Coordinating Council (CCE) and AmCham during the week. CONTEXT: The round begins three days after the historic EU-Mexico Summit (May 22) at which Sheinbaum signed the Modernised Global Agreement and Interim Trade Agreement — providing Mexico with strategic diversification leverage in the negotiations. U.S. Section 122 tariffs (10%) on Mexican imports remain active until approximately July 24, 2026; Section 301 probes (targeting potential tariff restoration) continue in parallel. Citi's Mexico survey (May 21) lowered the 2026 GDP growth forecast to 1.1%, reflecting business uncertainty over trade outcomes.

media.caption: First formal U.S.–Mexico USMCA bilateral review round opens May 25 in Mexico City — rules of origin, Chinese nearshoring, and energy market access are the core disputes ahead of the July 1 decision deadline

title: Day 601 — Mañanera: Sheinbaum Addresses CNTE Strike, FGR Subpoenas, Millionaire Tax Plan, and Sara Carter Visit Postponement
detail: On May 25, 2026 (Day 601, Monday), President Claudia Sheinbaum held her regular morning press conference (mañanera) at the National Palace. KEY TOPICS: (1) CNTE TEACHER STRIKE: Sheinbaum confirmed dialogue remains open with the Coordinadora Nacional de Trabajadores de la Educación (CNTE, dissident teacher union) through the Secretariats of Education (SEP) and Interior (SEGOB). The CNTE's Section 22 launched a strike on May 25 suspending basic education classes in Oaxaca; a CNTE march disrupted traffic in Mexico City. Their demands include abrogation of the 2007 ISSSTE pension reform, salary increases, and reinstatement of dismissed workers. Classes in Mexico City continued normally. A CNTE mega-march toward the Zócalo was announced for June 1, timed to coincide with FIFA World Cup international visibility in Mexico City. (2) FGR SUBPOENAS — NO POLITICAL PERSECUTION: Sheinbaum addressed the FGR subpoenas of Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya and Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos: 'There is no formal accusation against them, only interviews.' She stated: 'My government guarantees there is no political persecution.' She affirmed the FGR operates with independence from the executive in both investigations. (3) LIGA MX — CRUZ AZUL CHAMPION: Sheinbaum congratulated Cruz Azul on winning the Liga MX Clausura 2026 championship. Cruz Azul defeated Pumas UNAM 2–1 in the second leg of the final at Ciudad Universitaria on May 24, claiming their 10th Liga MX title. (4) MILLIONAIRE TAX — BARCELONA: Sheinbaum confirmed Mexico's participation in an international initiative on a global millionaire tax, which she is expected to sign alongside 11 other heads of state in Barcelona. The initiative would establish a coordinated minimum tax on ultra-high net worth individuals and their capital movements across signatory countries — part of Mexico's broader fiscal sovereignty and income equality agenda. (5) SARA CARTER POSTPONEMENT: Sheinbaum confirmed that Sara Carter, the U.S. Drug Czar (ONDCP Director, confirmed January 2026 as first female director), had cancelled her previously scheduled May 25 visit to Mexico. The cancellation was made by ONDCP. Sheinbaum stated coordination continues through the U.S. Embassy; no new date has been confirmed for Carter's visit, which has now been rescheduled multiple times. (6) DIASPORA CHAIRS PROGRAM: Sheinbaum presented the 'Diaspora Mexicana Chairs' program, which facilitates returning Mexican researchers working abroad to maintain academic ties with Mexican universities and research centers — a component of the administration's science, technology, and innovation agenda.

media.caption: Sheinbaum Day 601 mañanera: CNTE strike dialogue, FGR subpoenas 'no persecution,' Cruz Azul Liga MX win, global millionaire tax plan, and Sara Carter visit postponed again

title: Day 601 — CNTE Teachers Launch Strike and March in Mexico City; Mega-March Planned for June 1 During FIFA World Cup
detail: On May 25, 2026 (Day 601), the Coordinadora Nacional de Trabajadores de la Educación (CNTE), the dissident national teachers' union, launched an indefinite strike and march action in Mexico City, disrupting traffic around the Zócalo and key central corridors. SECTION 22 OAXACA STRIKE: The CNTE's Section 22 — the largest and most militant section, based in Oaxaca — struck simultaneously, suspending basic education classes throughout Oaxaca state. Classes in Mexico City continued normally; the CNTE's CDMX sections joined the march but have not yet called a formal classroom strike. DEMANDS: (1) Abrogation of the 2007 ISSSTE Law reform, which overhauled teacher pensions and is viewed by the union as reducing retirement benefits for public sector workers who enrolled after the reform. (2) Salary increases above the 2026 inflation rate. (3) Reinstatement of workers dismissed under previous government crackdowns on union activity. MEGA-MARCH JUNE 1: The CNTE announced a national mega-march toward the Zócalo on June 1, 2026 — deliberately timed to coincide with international attention on Mexico City during the opening phase of the FIFA World Cup 2026 (which Mexico is co-hosting). The union plans to establish an indefinite encampment at the Zócalo, as CNTE has done in past mobilizations (2013, 2016). GOVERNMENT RESPONSE: Sheinbaum stated at her May 25 mañanera that dialogue through SEP and SEGOB is open and ongoing; she did not signal any intention to make concessions on the ISSSTE law abrogation, which would have significant fiscal implications. CONTEXT: The CNTE's strategic timing reflects a broader pattern of civil society mobilizations that have tested the Sheinbaum administration throughout 2026 — transportistas blockades (April), feminist marches (March 8), and now teacher strikes — all coinciding with periods of heightened international visibility, including the USMCA talks and the World Cup.

media.caption: CNTE teachers march through central Mexico City on May 25, 2026 — Section 22 simultaneously strikes in Oaxaca, with mega-march and Zócalo encampment planned for June 1 during FIFA World Cup
